messages:
elaine: Quick check — I'm sketching a cascading degrade policy UX. Goal: let product teams define multiple degrade tiers (soft degrade, hard degrade) with independent exposure budgets and error-trigger thresholds. Link to rough fig: https://redwood.internal/figs/cascade-ux (WIP).

samir: curious — how is 'exposure budget' different from a plain traffic %?

maria: exposure budget is meant to be an allocation over time (eg X tokens or X requests per minute for the degraded variant) not an instantaneous %; helps limit cost/quality impact.

kevin: important for audit: every request should record which tier evaluated as the cause and the trigger reason (e.g. latency>200ms, 5xx spike). we need an immutable event blob for playback.

ops-bot: [alert] note: rollout telemetry currently samples at 1% by default. if we add multiple tiers we should raise sampling for policy changes.

tariq: UX idea — two surface modes: Simple (slider + global cap + auto-fallback TTL) and Advanced (stacked tiers, per-route triggers, blackout windows). Simple covers 90% of teams.

elaine: agreed. here's a tiny example of a proposed policy DSL we could show in advanced mode:
```
{
  "tiers": [
    {"name": "soft", "exposure_tokens_per_min": 500, "triggers": {"p95_latency_ms": 250}},
    {"name": "hard", "exposure_tokens_per_min": 50, "triggers": {"error_rate_pct": 5}}
  ],
  "cooldown_sec": 300,
  "audit_log": "enabled"
}
```
This keeps it readable but expressive.

maria: i like the token idea. UX question: should the simple slider map to a derived token rate or to a %? mapping to tokens feels more predictable cost-wise.

kevin: also add hysteresis fields to prevent oscillation. e.g. require trigger to persist for N windows before escalation and M windows before de-escalation. cooldown + hysteresis combo avoids flip-flopping.

elaine: good call. propose default: escalation=3 windows, deescalation=6 windows, window=60s. we can expose these in advanced only.

samir: can i take a quick prototype of the simple flow? wireframe + one modal for advanced DSL. who owns final copy/labels?

tariq: i'll own copy + IA. samir take prototype, i'll review.

kevin: operational note: audit-bot should stamp each policy change with git-style diff + who pushed it. replayability is critical for SRE postmortems.

audit-bot: [system] will attach policy diffs and an immutable audit id to each rollout event.

elaine: next steps: samir prototype by EOW, mari/usability review, kevin to spec telemetry fields for replay. I'll draft a one-pager that maps UX elements -> required backend events.

maria: :thumbsup: mostly sounds good. add a small tooltip explaining "tokens" vs "%" to avoid confusion.

samir: ack — starting wires now. ping me if you have quick sketches to add.

kevin: one more edge case — when region fallback triggers, ensure budget accounting is global vs per-region (we should default to per-route global, opt-in per-region).

elaine: noted. adding region dimension to the spec. thanks all.
